extracted.intended_audience: program sponsors, Registration Agencies (OA and SAAs), State CTE Agencies, employers participating in CTE apprenticeship programs, and public commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance and proposed requirements governing the design, agreements, administration, review, and oversight of registered CTE apprenticeship programs (subpart B), including required apprenticeship agreement elements, sponsor adoption agreements, Registration Agency responsibilities, and related protections for CTE apprentices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor standards adoption agreement (§29.24(d)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Prescribes the content and operational requirements for a written sponsor standards adoption agreement, as defined in proposed §29.2, between a sponsor and a participating employer that is reached outside of a collective bargaining process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended because employers are not eligible sponsors in this model; inclusion of a regulatory provision obligates participating employers to comply with the sponsor's standards of registered CTE apprenticeship and to adhere to the requirements contained in 29 CFR parts 29 and 30, bolstering program accountability and protecting apprentices' safety and welfare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement requirement (foundational) (§29.24(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: All registered CTE apprenticeship programs must develop an apprenticeship agreement containing the terms and conditions of the training and instruction plan for CTE apprentices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agreement is a foundational element to protect apprentices' welfare, establish transparency and accountability, explain program purpose/benefits/outcomes, and clarify training and instruction plans; for CTE apprenticeship it must include the program's terms and conditions for education in addition to employment and training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required signatories for apprenticeship agreement (§29.24(e)(1)(i)-(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: The apprenticeship agreement must be signed by the CTE apprentice; the CTE apprentice's parent or legal guardian if under 18; the sponsor; the secondary or postsecondary educational institution where the CTE apprentice is enrolled; and any participating employers that have adopted or agreed to the sponsor standards adoption agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addition of educational institution as a required signatory reflects the educational context and extends transparency/accountability to institutions; requiring institution signature also confirms apprentice eligibility via enrollment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of signed agreement prior to start (§29.24(e)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The signed apprenticeship agreement (including the program standards) must be provided to the CTE apprentice and their parent or legal guardian, as applicable, prior to the apprenticeship's start date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures parents/guardians of school-aged participants are informed about hourly demands, safety/welcoming assurances, and what the apprentice can expect to receive to support professional development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact and identifying information element (§29.24(e)(3)(i)-(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Apprenticeship agreements must include contact and identifying information for CTE apprentices (including date of birth and, on a voluntary basis, Social Security number) and contact information for the Registration Agency, sponsor, and any participating employers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SSN is voluntary on agreement but needed by employer; these elements ensure the agreement is a reliable source for up-to-date contact information for participants and program administrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Occupation, industry skills framework, and instruction outline (§29.24(e)(3)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreements must identify the job or occupation the CTE apprentice will be employed in, as well as the industry skills framework and CTE apprenticeship-related instruction outline that underpin alignment with an established CTE course of study and a career readiness framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mirrors work process schedule for registered apprenticeship but uses terminology appropriate to CTE model to clarify program alignment with CTE coursework and career readiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program standards element (§29.24(e)(3)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: The apprenticeship agreement must include the program's standards for the registered CTE apprenticeship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures the agreement contains the sponsor's standards applicable to CTE apprentices and clarifies expected behaviors, curricula, and training standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roles, duties, and responsibilities element (§29.24(e)(3)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreements must describe the roles, duties, and responsibilities of CTE apprentices, sponsors, and participating employers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires participating employers to provide CTE apprentices information about their rights and protections under Federal, State, and local labor laws and the process for filing complaints with the Registration Agency; promotes accountability and worker protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term dates and probationary period element (§29.24(e)(3)(vi))
rubrics_metrics.description: The apprenticeship agreement must provide the beginning and expected end date for the term, the date when on-the-job training will begin, and a description of the program's probationary period, which may not exceed 30 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differs from registered apprenticeship (which allows longer/more flexible probationary periods); 30-day cap reflects that CTE apprentices are enrolled in established CTE programs and need shorter probation for their interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wages and wage progression element (§29.24(e)(3)(vii))
rubrics_metrics.description: The apprenticeship agreement must include the entry wage and graduated scale of increasing wages for registered CTE apprentices; it would not include 'journeyworker wage' nor 'fringe benefits' information as required for registered apprenticeship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CTE model focuses on industry skills frameworks and may relate to multiple occupations, so journeyworker wages are not required; Department encourages employers to invest in apprentices with wages/fringe benefits when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of hours element (§29.24(e)(3)(viii))
rubrics_metrics.description: The agreement must contain the allocation of hours between on-the-job training and CTE apprenticeship-related instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mirrors registered apprenticeship requirement but uses 'CTE apprenticeship-related instruction' term to reflect educational component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competency measurement methods element (§29.24(e)(3)(ix))
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreements must explain the methods used over the course of the program to measure CTE apprentices' attainment of competencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike registered apprenticeship, registered CTE apprenticeship does not include an end-point assessment; programs have flexibility to design completion measures appropriate to associated career pathways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive services description (§29.24(e)(3)(x))
rubrics_metrics.description: Apprenticeship agreements should describe any supportive services available to apprentices (e.g., childcare services, transportation stipends, equipment/tools).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provision of supportive services helps address participation barriers (particularly for underserved or rural communities); Department requests comment on whether programs should be required to provide access to supportive services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unreimbursed costs disclosure (§29.24(e)(3)(xi))
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreements must contain a description of the nature and amount of any unreimbursed costs associated with the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department is concerned about excessive participation costs; proposed requirement discloses all participation costs to prevent unexpected burdens on participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credentials, credits, or postsecondary hours disclosure (§29.24(e)(3)(xii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreements must include a description of any credentials, secondary credits, or postsecondary credit hours conferred upon participants who progress through the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For CTE apprenticeship, text would not refer to 'occupational qualifications' or licensure; Department expects CTE programs may confer secondary credits or at least 12 postsecondary credit hours that accelerate educational progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to parts 29 and 30 affirmation (§29.24(e)(3)(xiii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreements must include an affirmation from all parties that they will adhere to the applicable requirements of parts 29 and 30 governing registered apprenticeship and EEO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reiterates that, except when explicitly stated otherwise, parts 29 and 30 requirements apply to any apprenticeship program registered for Federal purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation for instruction statement (§29.24(e)(3)(xiv))
rubrics_metrics.description: The agreement must state whether the CTE apprenticeship-related instruction component is paid and, if so, what the wage rate is, and whether the instruction is provided during work hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides transparency on paid vs. unpaid instruction and timing so apprentices can make financial decisions and seek supportive services; Department encourages wages during instruction where possible and sponsors must consider paying wages for instruction when developing program standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint contact information element (§29.24(e)(3)(xv))
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreements must contain contact information of those individuals or entities designated by the program to receive, review, and address any controversies or complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps apprentices understand the process for filing, reviewing, and resolving complaints and whom to contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: FERPA consent for disclosure of apprentice information (§29.24(e)(3)(xvi))
rubrics_metrics.description: The agreement must include consent permitting the secondary or postsecondary institution to disclose individual apprentice-level information to the program sponsor, intermediary sponsor-designating entity, participating employers, Registration Agency, the Department, and other institutions involved in administering the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures institutions receiving Federal education funds can meet FERPA obligations (parent/eligible student written consent) and disclose information as required; special FERPA considerations apply for minors and eligible students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on non-compete provisions (§29.24(e)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Apprenticeship agreements must prohibit any non-compete provisions or other provisions that would serve to restrict an apprentice's labor market mobility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department views prohibition of non-competes as a key reform to maximize training benefits and protect apprentices' future employment opportunities across both registered apprenticeship and registered CTE apprenticeship models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on non-disclosure provisions that restrict mobility (§29.24(e)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Apprenticeship agreements must prohibit non-disclosure provisions that would serve to restrict an apprentice's labor market mobility and future success finding employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No exemption for registered CTE apprenticeship programs; restrictions could disproportionately harm early-career CTE apprentices who may be at risk of career consequences from such clauses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission timeline for executed agreements (§29.24(e)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered CTE apprenticeship program sponsors must submit a completed copy of the executed apprenticeship agreement for each individual apprentice it registers to the Registration Agency within 30 days of execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This proposed 30-day timeframe is a reduction from prior policy (45 days) and is reasonable given technological advancements (RAPIDS); aligns timelines across CTE and regular registered apprenticeship models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificates of completion (§29.24(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration Agencies would issue certificates of completion of registered CTE apprenticeship to CTE apprentices who complete all program requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificates are important milestones that signify value in the job market; registered apprenticeship programs in subpart A may consider providing advanced standing to CTE apprentices who can demonstrate completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration Agency administrative duties (general) (§29.24(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration Agencies operating registered CTE apprenticeship programs must satisfy administrative requirements addressing core duties: technical assistance, program registration, processes for CTE apprentices, operation of program reviews, deregistration processes, recognition of Registration Agencies, data collection/metrics, and program exemptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section structures Registration Agency roles/responsibilities to support program quality and alignment with State/local education systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: 90-day decision period for registration (§29.24(g)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration Agency must make a determination within 90 days of receipt of a complete application as to whether the program has met the subpart requirements and is eligible for registration; must inform applicants in writing of decisions and explain reasons for denial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a transparent, time-bound process for sponsors and Registration Agencies for review and approval of programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration Agency role in technical assistance and outreach (§29.24(g)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration Agencies are responsible for providing technical assistance and other support, including outreach, technical assistance, and referrals to registered apprenticeship programs under subpart A to sponsors or potential partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports adoption and expansion of registered CTE apprenticeship programs in a State and encourages coordination with existing apprenticeship programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint handling and referral to State CTE Agency (§29.24(g)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: CTE apprentice complaints follow a process similar to §29.17; Registration Agency may refer complaints to the State CTE Agency as appropriate due to close coordination envisioned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referrals should be addressed in written agreement between Registration Agency and State CTE Agency; aims to route certain education-related complaints to the entity best positioned to resolve them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program review process and coordination (§29.24(g)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Program reviews will follow the process in §29.19 and should be coordinated between the Registration Agency and the State CTE Agency; examples include State CTE Agency reviewing CTE portions while Registration Agency reviews labor standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department allows flexibility on how coordination occurs but expects a strategy/agreement; joint reviews encouraged though not required; program reviews under this subpart do not affect Perkins program eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on Registration Agency authority relative to Perkins programs (§29.24(g)(4)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Program reviews under this subpart would not impact an entity's eligibility under, or compliance with, Perkins programs; Registration Agency authority is limited to registration of the program and does not extend to determining CTE funding eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies separation between apprenticeship registration functions and Perkins statute-administered CTE program eligibility under ED.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deregistration process for noncompliance (§29.24(g)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides for deregistration of programs that fail to meet the requirements of this subpart and part 30; process would be the same as proposed §29.20 of subpart A, typically following a program review to ascertain compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deregistration is critical to effective oversight; Department welcomes comments on aligning deregistration proceedings with subpart A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearings on deregistration and related processes (§29.24(g)(6)-(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration and deregistration hearings processes for CTE apprenticeship would align with those described in §29.21 of subpart A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aligning administrative processes minimizes parallel procedures across subparts; Department seeks comment on whether deviations would provide administrative efficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition and qualification of Registration Agencies (§29.24(g)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration Agencies for CTE apprenticeship may be OA or a recognized SAA; given the written agreement requirement with the State CTE Agency, OA would only serve as Registration Agency where OA has not recognized an SAA and there is a written agreement with the State CTE Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department envisions local registration aligning with State/local education systems and does not anticipate national program registration models for this subpart; adoption of subpart B is not required to obtain or maintain SAA recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAA recognition process to register CTE apprenticeship programs (§29.24(g)(8)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: SAAs may seek recognition for the registration of CTE apprenticeship programs through the process outlined in proposed regulatory text (§29.24(g)(8)(ii)(A)-(D)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details of the recognition process (A–D) are provided to enable SAAs to apply for recognition to register CTE apprenticeship programs; Department is open to comments on recognition and national registration models.
